title: Yŏja sanghaeng pʻyŏn
shelf_note: Hangul cursive (궁체-like) manuscript on women's conduct, 18th c.; belongs on a Korean shelf.
structure_note: Counts are clean (62 records, 62 distinct, all OCR'd); only 33/62 translated. The OCR on 3 of 4 sampled pages collapses into a repeated word (됴흔, 비록) or a repeated sentence block, so the untranslated remainder and the 'skip' on p48 are symptoms of failed OCR, not of a structural splice.

book_verdict: The OCR does not read this cursive Hangul manuscript: one page is a loose modern-Korean paraphrase and three pages collapse into loops or invented maxims. The English then translates the loops, and on one page it explains the loop as a calligraphy exercise.
reader_summary: A cursive Hangul manuscript of conduct rules for women. The transcription is not this manuscript's text: one page is approximate, and the others repeat a word or an invented sentence for most of the page. The English cannot be trusted on any sampled page.

title: Hanʾgwa
shelf_note: Korean manuscript anthology of examination-style 表/賀/謝 compositions in Classical Chinese with red and blue reading marks; Korean literati material.
structure_note: Counts are clean (150/150, 135 translated). The language field says Korean, but the text is Classical Chinese, so that field is wrong for this book (minor). On all four sampled images the lower half of the leaf is a blocky, low-resolution band where the small double-column text cannot be read; this looks like a fault in the stored image, not in the original.

The translation invents people from misreadings (p13, p57) and writes fluent prose over character noise (p95). p133, a page of large text only, is sound.
reader_summary: A Korean manuscript anthology of model congratulatory and thanks pieces (賀/謝) in Classical Chinese, with titles drawn from Zhou-to-Ming history. The large titles and main lines are mostly transcribed correctly. The small commentary is not reliably read, and the English invents names and passages where the transcription fails.

title: Tʻonggam chu, Sŏhan chi odae

structure_note: Counts are clean (126/126, 118 translated). The 3 backsteps and 9 repeats among only 13 printed numbers probably come from the OCR reading cyclical-year headwords (壬午, 癸未…) or volume references as page numbers, not from a scan fault. p23 has large later characters brushed over the text (practice writing), and p38 has a pixelated band at the foot.

book_verdict: The right text is transcribed in outline, and many headwords are correct. But meaning-changing misreads are common (犢→懷, 土星→去皇), whole notes are invented on p23, and the English turns glosses into invented people and books.
reader_summary: A Korean manuscript word-list and commentary to the Zizhi tongjian, with headwords in large script and glosses in small double columns. The transcription follows the right text but misreads many glosses and invents some. The English is usable only as a pointer to the headwords; names and glosses must be checked against the image.

title: Sinpʻyŏn Sanhak kyemong
shelf_note: Korean (c.1660) edition of Zhu Shijie's Suanxue qimeng, the core mathematics textbook of Joseon.
structure_note: Counts are nearly complete (167/168 OCR'd, 154 translated). The 4 backsteps among 17 printed numbers are most likely misread leaf numerals (p81 carries 三九 in the margin), not a scan fault. The edition is printed, but the OCR labels some pages 'handwritten' (minor, O16). Some images have a pixelated horizontal band.

book_verdict: The right text in a clear print, but the transcription misreads or drops numbers on every sampled page (32→33, a missing question, wrong totals, missing fractions). In a mathematics book this breaks the problems, and on p81 the two panes give different figures.
reader_summary: The Korean edition of Zhu Shijie's Suanxue qimeng (Introduction to Mathematics), problems with answers and methods. The transcription is of the right text, but its numbers are unreliable: answers, totals and fractions are misread or dropped. The English follows the problems' logic well, but every figure must be checked against the image.
